title: G
full_review:
Apart from a 1926 silent version, there have been two major screen adaptations of "The Great Gatsby": one in 1949 staring Alan Ladd and another in 1974 with Robert Redford in the title role. Both were disappointing.

The same can be said of "G" (Andrew Lauren Productions), a tepid updating of F. Scott Fitzgerald's Jazz Age classic.

Set amid the affluence of the Hamptons on Long Island, N.Y., the triangular tragic love story centers on the Gatsby-like Summer G (Richard T. Jones), here a tormented hip-hop mogul still passionately in love with the woman (Chenoa Maxwell, this film's Daisy) who left him 10 years earlier and is now the unhappily married trophy wife of a rich but unfaithful Wall Street executive (Blair Underwood).

Despite a solid performance by Jones, the low-budget movie is weighed down by a flat, melodramatic script riddled with decidedly un-"G"-rated dialogue.

The film contains an adulterous sexual encounter, brief violence and pervasive rough and sexually crude language. The USCCB Office for Film & Broadcasting classification is L -- limited adult audience, films whose problematic content many adults would find troubling. The Motion Picture Association of America rating is R -- restricted.
